chunks: Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Khaybari, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in the early days of the reign of Abu Ja'far, so he stayed in Najaf. He said: O Musa! Go to the main road and stand there and look, for a man will come to you from the direction of al-Qadisiyyah. When he comes close to you, say to him: 'Here is a man from the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who is calling you,' and he will come with you.

He said: So I went until I stood on the road, and the heat was intense. I kept standing until I was about to disobey [the Imam] and leave, when I saw something approaching that resembled a man on a camel. I kept looking at him until he came close to me, and I said: O this man, here is a man from the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who is calling you, and he has described you to me. He said: Take us to him.

He said: So I brought him until he made his camel rest in a place near the tent. The Imam called for him, so the Arab entered to him. I came close and stood at the door of the tent, hearing the speech but not seeing them.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked him: From where did you come? He said: From the furthest part of Yemen. He said: Are you from such and such place? He said: Yes, I am from such and such place.
He said: What brought you here? He said: I came to visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: So you came without a specific need, solely for the visitation?
He said: I came without a need, except that I pray near him and visit him, so I may send greetings to him and return to my family.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: And what do you believe regarding his visitation? He said: We believe that in his visitation there is blessing for ourselves, our families, our children, our wealth, our livelihood, and the fulfillment of our needs.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Shall I not add to you from his virtue a virtue, O brother of Yemen? He said: Add to me, O son of the Messenger of Allah.
He said: Verily, the visitation of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equals one accepted, pure Hajj with the Messenger of Allah. He was amazed by that.
He said: Yes, by Allah, and two accepted, pure, and pure Hajjs with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He was amazed.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) kept increasing [the number] until he said: Thirty accepted, pure, and pure Hajjs with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of visiting Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narrative from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) engages a Yemeni pilgrim to highlight the spiritual magnitude of visiting Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), progressively elevating the reward from one to thirty accepted Hajjs performed alongside the Prophet. This cumulative increase underscores the Shia scholarly view that Ziyarah is not merely a commemorative act but a profound spiritual transaction that compensates for the lack of direct companionship with the Prophet. The story serves as a foundational text for the theological emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt’s intercessory and merit-generating role in the afterlife.
